title: Prime number
summary: A prime is a natural number greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself.

context.framework: positive natural numbers with ordinary multiplication and order
context.note: Revision 3 keeps the integer and natural-number scopes consistent and expands divisibility inside the statement.

assumptions.text: The natural-number structure and its ordinary multiplication are fixed.

content.plain: A prime is greater than one and cannot be written as a product except using one or itself.
content.exact: Let 1:=S(0). For p∈N, Prime(p) iff p>1 and for every d∈N, if there exists k∈N with p=d·k, then d=1 or d=p.
content.example: 7 is prime. 12 is not prime because 12=3·4 and 3 is neither 1 nor 12.
content.caveat: This is the positive-natural-number definition. Prime elements in general rings require units and associates to be specified.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Corrects the former Z-versus-positive-natural scope mismatch and makes the divisibility predicate explicit. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
